content.text: Spring Framework is the dominant application framework in the Java ecosystem, providing a comprehensive programming and configuration model for enterprise applications. Built on the principles of Inversion of Control (IoC) and Dependency Injection (DI), Spring eliminates boilerplate code while enabling modular, testable, and maintainable architectures. Spring Boot extends the core framework with opinionated defaults, embedded servers, and auto-configuration that dramatically accelerates development from prototype to production.

This guide covers Spring from core container concepts through production deployment patterns, targeting senior engineers building microservices, event-driven systems, and enterprise integrations. Each subtopic provides deep coverage of a specific Spring module with production-oriented examples, common pitfalls, and interview preparation material.

items: Core Container and Dependency Injection — IoC container, bean lifecycle, scopes, profiles, and configuration patterns
Spring Boot — Auto-configuration, embedded servers, actuator, and production-ready application setup
Spring MVC and REST APIs — Web layer architecture, request handling, validation, error handling, and API design
Spring REST — RESTful API design, content negotiation, HATEOAS, and API versioning patterns
Spring Data and Persistence — JPA repositories, query methods, transactions, and database access patterns
Spring Security — Authentication, authorization, OAuth2, JWT, and security filter chain configuration
Spring Cloud and Microservices — Service discovery, circuit breakers, distributed configuration, and API gateway patterns
Spring Batch — Batch processing, chunk-oriented steps, job scheduling, and large-scale data operations
